amendment_reason: v1 falsely identified ker(V-1) with E(F_p)=ker(pi-1), so its observed-pole product omitted denominator factors whose roots did not split in the frozen extension; v2 jointly reconstructs numerator and denominator without assuming split poles
question: Does joint degree-(N,N-1) rational interpolation recover one extension-stable base-field x-map for [t-1]P-pi(P), and do observed kernel points follow the new Frobenius-eigenspace prediction gcd(N,(t-1)^d-1)?

degree_model.denominator_degree: N-1 with leading coefficient normalized to one
degree_model.sample_requirement: at least 2*N regular x-values for reconstruction and strictly more than 2*N-1 for separation

kernel_eigenspace_model.premise: on ker(V-1), V=1 and therefore pi=[t-1]
kernel_eigenspace_model.predicted_distinct_pole_x: floor(predicted_visible_kernel_size/2) for the cyclic kernels in this panel

reconstruction.equations: N(x_i)=image_x_i*D(x_i) with deg N<=N, deg D=N-1, and leading(D)=1
reconstruction.first_window: first 2*N regular x-values in canonical field-index order
reconstruction.second_window: last 2*N regular x-values in canonical field-index order
reconstruction.solver: deterministic Gaussian elimination over GF(p^d), requiring a unique pivot in every column
reconstruction.validation: evaluate both candidates on every regular sample and every observed pole; require base-field coefficients and cross-degree separation margin

independent_verifier.method: separate Python field/group implementation and Gaussian solver

positive_checks: paired points above each x have equal image x-coordinate or both map to infinity
observed pole multiplicity plus infinity equals gcd(N,(t-1)^d-1) and the distinct pole count equals its frozen cyclic prediction
both 2*N-window linear systems have unique solutions and recover identical degree-(N,N-1) candidates
all recovered coefficients lie in F_p and are identical across extension degrees of each base curve
both candidates match every regular sample, their denominator vanishes at every observed pole, and their numerator does not cancel any observed pole
the regular sample count is strictly greater than the cross degree 2*N-1
controls: adding one to the numerator constant rejects every regular sample
adding one to the denominator constant destroys every observed pole
exactly 2*N-1 samples fail the strict separation-cardinality premise
the retained v1 split-pole reconstruction remains failed and is not overwritten
measurements: predicted and observed visible-kernel size, pole multiplicity and distinct pole count
solver ranks, degrees, coefficient encodings, full-sample mismatch and pole-cancellation counts
strict separation margin and mutation rejection counts
producer and verifier elapsed nanoseconds as single-run diagnostics

acceptance.primary: all positive checks pass in all eight cells, every exact field matches independent replay, and all three base-curve coefficient families are stable
acceptance.controls: all controls reject or expose the intended boundary in every applicable cell
acceptance.failure_policy: retain every row; do not replace any v1 or v2 cell, window, degree, eigenspace prediction, check, or control

claim_boundary: V2 tests a corrected finite-panel degree, eigenspace and rational-reconstruction model. It does not prove cyclicity or deg(V-1)=N generically, identify a scheme morphism over the algebraic closure, transport equality to completed local series, solve ECDLP, or establish runtime or asymptotic improvement.
